blocks.text: Read the chapter with this setting in view: John's predicated and absolute ego eimi sayings participate in characterization through ordinary identification, symbolic predicates, scriptural echoes, and divine-agency claims; each context must be read separately. It gives a starting point for following the chapter's own movement. The chapter itself should determine how far the point is taken. A more precise reconstruction remains disputed.

For its historical and cultural setting, note that John 7:53-8:11 is absent from the earliest major Greek witnesses, appears at different locations in later transmission, and is widely judged not part of the earliest recoverable form of John even though it has a long reception as Scripture. This background clarifies the setting assumed by the passage. It does not by itself settle every question raised by the chapter. Interpretations differ on some details.
